med-dimenhydrinate.dose_text: 1-2 tablets (50 mg each) every 4-6 h; first dose 30-60 min before travel; max 8 tablets per 24 h (label).

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Dimenhydrinate
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-dimenhydrinate.note: Interval 4 h agrees (label 4-6 h; MedlinePlus every 4-8 h by age). mg and 24 h maximum are label-only (MedlinePlus gives no mg), so left null.

med-simethicone.dose_text: Chew 1-2 tablets (125 mg each) as needed after meals and at bedtime; max 4 tablets per 24 h (label).

sources.name: DailyMed: TopCare® Extra Strength Gas Relief 48 Chewable Tablets
MedlinePlus: Simethicone
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-simethicone.note: MedlinePlus confirms after meals and at bedtime (four times a day) but gives no mg; Label-only figures kept in dose_text; numeric fields left null because the second source does not state them.

med-peg-3350.dose_text: 17 g powder dissolved in 4-8 oz of drink, once a day; do not use more than 7 days (label).

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Polyethylene Glycol 3350
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-peg-3350.note: Once daily agrees (MedlinePlus). 17 g dose is label-only, so mg/amount left null. Label: do not use with kidney disease unless a doctor advises.

med-bismuth.dose_text: Chew 2 tablets (262 mg each) every 30-60 min as needed; max 8 doses (16 tablets) in 24 h (label).

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Bismuth Subsalicylate
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-bismuth.note: MedlinePlus says follow the package; gives no dose or interval. Label-only figures kept in dose_text; numeric fields left null because the second source does not state them. Label: do not use with bloody or black stool, ulcer or bleeding problem.

med-cephalexin.dose_text: 500 mg every 12 hours (label alternative to 250 mg every 6 h) for 7-14 days.
med-cephalexin.renal: Dose adjustment needed if CrCl < 30 mL/min (label).

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Cephalexin
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-cephalexin.note: Label 250 mg q6h or 500 mg q12h (up to 4 g/day for severe infection); NHS 500 mg 2-3 times a day; MedlinePlus every 6 or 12 h. Used conservative 500 mg q12h; maxDaily null (4 g is label-only).

med-metronidazole.dose_text: Label: 7.5 mg/kg (about 500 mg for 70 kg) every 6 h, max 4 g per 24 h, usually 7-10 days.
med-metronidazole.hepatic: Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C): reduce dose by 50% (label).

sources.name: DailyMed: Metronidazole Tablets USP
sources.section: Dosage and Administration: Anaerobic Bacterial Infections

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Metronidazole
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-metronidazole.note: Interval disagreement: label every 6 h, MedlinePlus 2-4 times daily, NHS usually 2-3 times a day; conservative 8 h used. mg/kg and 4 g maximum are label-only (not in second source), so null.

med-metoclopramide.dose_text: Label (gastroparesis): 10 mg 30 min before each meal and at bedtime, max 40 mg per day.
med-metoclopramide.renal: Label recommends reduced dosage in moderate-severe renal impairment.
med-metoclopramide.hepatic: Label recommends reduced dosage in moderate-severe hepatic impairment.
med-metoclopramide.elderly: Label recommends reduced dosage in elderly patients.

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Metoclopramide
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-metoclopramide.note: Interval disagreement: MedlinePlus 4 times a day; NHS up to 3 times a day with at least 6 h between doses; conservative 6 h used. mg and 40 mg/day maximum are label-only, so null.

med-prochlorperazine.dose_text: Label: usually 5 mg or 10 mg tablet 3 or 4 times daily; daily doses above 40 mg only in resistant cases.
med-prochlorperazine.elderly: Lower range usually sufficient; more prone to hypotension and neuromuscular reactions (label).

sources.name: DailyMed: Prochlorperazine Maleate Tablets, USP Rx only
sources.section: Dosage and Administration: Severe Nausea and Vomiting

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Prochlorperazine
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-prochlorperazine.note: Frequency disagreement: label 3-4 times daily, MedlinePlus 1-4 times, NHS 2-3 times a day; no common minimum interval stated in hours, so interval null. mg label-only.

med-clindamycin.dose_text: Label: 150-300 mg every 6 h (serious infections); 300-450 mg every 6 h (more severe). Take with a full glass of water.

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Clindamycin
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-clindamycin.note: Interval 6 h agrees (label every 6 h; MedlinePlus 3-4 times a day). mg is label-only, so null.

med-oseltamivir.dose_text: Treatment: 75 mg twice daily for 5 days. Prevention: 75 mg once daily for at least 10 days (label).
med-oseltamivir.renal: CrCl >30-60 mL/min: 30 mg twice daily; CrCl >10-30: 30 mg once daily (label).

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Oseltamivir
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-oseltamivir.note: Twice daily for 5 days agrees (MedlinePlus). 75 mg is label-only (MedlinePlus gives no mg), so mg null.

med-tramadol.dose_text: Label: 50-100 mg every 4-6 h as needed, not over 400 mg/day; start low (25 mg/day titration) when rapid onset not needed.
med-tramadol.renal: CrCl < 30 mL/min: every 12 h, max 200 mg/day (label).
med-tramadol.hepatic: Severe hepatic impairment: 50 mg every 12 h (label).

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Tramadol
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-tramadol.note: Interval agrees: label/MedlinePlus every 4-6 h; NHS 3-4 times a day. NHS lists 50 mg tablets but no dose or daily maximum, so mg/maxDaily null. Opioid: risk of respiratory depression (label boxed warning).

med-oxycodone.dose_text: Label: start 5-15 mg every 4-6 h as needed, lowest effective dose, shortest duration.

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Oxycodone
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-oxycodone.note: Every 4-6 h agrees (MedlinePlus). mg is label-only, so null. Opioid: life-threatening respiratory depression (label boxed warning).

med-cyclobenzaprine.dose_text: Label: 5 mg three times a day; may increase to 10 mg three times a day; not longer than 2-3 weeks.

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Cyclobenzaprine
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-cyclobenzaprine.note: Three times a day agrees (MedlinePlus). mg is label-only, so null.

med-ketorolac.indication: Moderate to severe pain (after IV/IM dose)
med-ketorolac.dose_text: Label: only as continuation after IV/IM; 20 mg once then 10 mg every 4-6 h, max 40 mg/day; total IV/IM/oral use max 5 days.
med-ketorolac.elderly: Age 65+ or weight < 50 kg: 10 mg first dose, max 40 mg/day (label).

sources.name: DailyMed: KETOROLAC TROMETHAMINE TABLETS USP, 10 mg Rx only
MedlinePlus: Ketorolac
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-ketorolac.note: Every 4-6 h agrees (MedlinePlus). mg and 40 mg/day max are label-only, so null.

med-metoprolol.dose_text: Label: start 100 mg/day in single or divided doses with meals; range 100-450 mg/day. NHS: 50-100 mg twice a day.

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Metoprolol
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-metoprolol.note: Conservative 50 mg twice daily (= label 100 mg/day divided; NHS 50-100 mg twice a day). maxDaily null: label 450 mg/day not stated by NHS. Tablet (tartrate) only; IV use for fast rhythm is not covered here.

med-furosemide.dose_text: Label: 20-80 mg as a single dose; may repeat or raise by 20-40 mg not sooner than 6-8 h later; then once or twice daily.

sources.name: DailyMed: Furosemide Tablets, USP 20 mg, 40 mg, and 80 mg Rx Only
MedlinePlus: Furosemide
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-furosemide.note: Interval disagreement: label allows a repeat after 6-8 h during titration; MedlinePlus usually once or twice a day; conservative 12 h used. mg is label-only, so null.

med-apixaban.dose_text: Label: DVT/PE treatment 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily.

sources.name: DailyMed: Eliquis (Apixaban) Tablet, Film Coated Eliquis 30-Day Starter Pack (Apixaban) Kit Eliquis (Apixaban) Tablet, For Suspension Eliquis Sprinkle (Apixaban) Capsule
MedlinePlus: Apixaban
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-apixaban.note: Twice daily agrees (MedlinePlus). mg is label-only, so null. Label: AF dose 2.5 mg twice daily if 2 of age >= 80, weight <= 60 kg, creatinine >= 1.5 mg/dL.

med-clopidogrel.dose_text: Single 300 mg loading dose, then 75 mg once daily (label).

sources.name: DailyMed: Clopidogrel Bisulfate Tablet, Film Coated
MedlinePlus: Clopidogrel
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-clopidogrel.note: 75 mg once daily agrees (NHS, MedlinePlus). NHS mentions one-off 300 mg or 600 mg; label loading dose is 300 mg, so maxSingle 300 (conservative). maxDaily null (not stated).

med-midodrine.dose_text: Label: 10 mg 3 times daily in daytime (about 4 h apart, not closer than 3 h); last dose before 6 PM.

gates.why: Supine hypertension risk; no experience above supine systolic 180 mmHg

sources.name: DailyMed: MIDODRINE HYDROCHLORIDE TABLET [MYLAN PHARMACEUTICALS INC.]
MedlinePlus: Midodrine
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-midodrine.note: 3 h minimum interval agrees (MedlinePlus: at least 3 hours apart). mg is label-only, so null. Gate threshold from label statement; measure BP lying down.

med-fludrocortisone.dose_text: Label covers Addison disease only: usual 0.1 mg daily. No labelled dose for orthostatic intolerance; flight surgeon to set.

sources.name: DailyMed: Fludrocortisone Acetate Tablets, USP (0.1 mg) Rx only
MedlinePlus: Fludrocortisone
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-fludrocortisone.note: Onboard use is off-label; neither source gives a dose for it and MedlinePlus gives no mg, so all numeric fields null.

med-diazepam.dose_text: Label: 2-10 mg 3-4 times daily (muscle spasm) or 2-4 times daily (anxiety).
med-diazepam.elderly: 2-2.5 mg once or twice daily initially (label).

sources.name: DailyMed: Diazepam Tablets, USP CIV Rx only
MedlinePlus: Diazepam
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-diazepam.note: Up to 4 times daily agrees (MedlinePlus 1-4 times a day), giving 6 h minimum. mg is label-only (NHS only gives an example split), so null. Seizure use (IV/rectal) not covered.

med-levetiracetam.dose_text: Label (adults 16+): 500 mg twice daily; increase by 500 mg twice daily every 2 weeks to 1500 mg twice daily.
med-levetiracetam.renal: Label requires dose adjustment by creatinine clearance.

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Levetiracetam
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-levetiracetam.note: Twice daily agrees (MedlinePlus, NHS once or twice a day). mg is label-only, so null.

med-trazodone.dose_text: Label (depression only): start 150 mg/day in divided doses, max 400 mg/day, after a meal. No labelled insomnia dose.

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Trazodone
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-trazodone.note: Onboard use for insomnia is off-label; neither source gives an insomnia dose, so numeric fields null.

med-bupropion.dose_text: Label (SR tablet): start 150 mg/day; after 3 days may go to 150 mg twice daily at least 8 h apart; max 400 mg/day.

sources.name: DailyMed: Bupropion Hydrochloride Tablet, Film Coated, Extended Release
MedlinePlus: Bupropion
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-bupropion.note: 8 h minimum interval is label; MedlinePlus says 1-4 times a day by formulation (consistent). mg and max are label-only, so null. Lowers seizure threshold (label).

med-enoxaparin.dose_text: Label: 1 mg/kg subcutaneously every 12 hours for DVT (outpatient, without PE).
med-enoxaparin.renal: Label requires dose adjustment if CrCl < 30 mL/min.

sources.name: DailyMed: Enoxaparin Sodium Injection,Usp Injection, Solution
MedlinePlus: Enoxaparin Injection
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-enoxaparin.note: Every 12 h agrees (MedlinePlus: twice a day). 1 mg/kg is label-only, so mg null and perKg false.

med-glucagon.indication: Severe low blood sugar when unable to swallow
med-glucagon.dose_text: 1 mg (1 mL) SC, IM or IV; if no response after 15 minutes, one more 1 mg dose while waiting for help (label).

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Glucagon Injection
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-glucagon.note: 15 min repeat agrees (MedlinePlus). mg is label-only (MedlinePlus gives no mg), so null. Kit label; nasal powder not covered.

med-dextrose-50.dose_text: Label: 10-25 g dextrose (20-50 mL of 50%) by slow IV injection; repeat if needed.
med-dextrose-50.note: No allowed second source found (no MedlinePlus or NHS page); all numeric fields null.

med-adenosine.dose_text: Label: 6 mg rapid IV bolus over 1-2 s with saline flush; if no effect in 1-2 min, 12 mg; 12 mg may be repeated once.
med-adenosine.note: No allowed second source found (no MedlinePlus or NHS page); all numeric fields null.

med-zoledronic-acid.dose_text: Label: 5 mg IV infusion over no less than 15 minutes, once a year (treatment) or once every 2 years (prevention).

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Zoledronic Acid Injection
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-zoledronic-acid.note: Once every 1-2 years agrees (MedlinePlus); 5 mg is label-only, so null. Interval in hours not meaningful.

med-guaifenesin.dose_text: 1-2 tablets (200 mg each) every 4 hours; max 6 doses in 24 h (label).

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Guaifenesin
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-guaifenesin.note: Every 4 h agrees (MedlinePlus). mg and daily maximum are label-only, so null.

med-dextromethorphan.dose_text: 2 tablets (15 mg each) every 6-8 hours as needed; max 8 tablets in 24 h (label).

sources.name: DailyMed: DEXTABS (DEXTROMETHORPHAN HYDROBROMIDE) TABLET [DXM PHARMACUETICAL, INC.]
MedlinePlus: Dextromethorphan
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-dextromethorphan.note: Label every 6-8 h; MedlinePlus every 4-12 h by product; 6 h used (label minimum, consistent). mg and max are label-only, so null.

med-tranexamic-acid.dose_text: Label (hemophilia dental extraction only): 10 mg/kg IV, infuse no faster than 1 mL/min. No labelled trauma dose.
med-tranexamic-acid.renal: Label: reduce dose in renal impairment.
med-tranexamic-acid.note: Onboard trauma-bleeding use is off-label; the NHS page covers tablets for heavy periods, so no second source for the IV dose. All numeric fields null.

med-scopolamine-patch.dose_text: Apply 1 patch behind one ear at least 4 h before needed; wear up to 3 days; then replace behind the other ear. One patch at a time.

sources.name: DailyMed: Scopolamine Transdermal System Patch, Extended Release
MedlinePlus: Scopolamine Transdermal Patch
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-scopolamine-patch.note: 1 patch, at least 4 h before travel, agrees across label and MedlinePlus; label: up to 3 days per patch (72 h). Label contraindication: angle-closure glaucoma.

med-silver-sulfadiazine.dose_text: After cleaning and debriding, apply about 1/16 inch layer once to twice daily; keep burn covered with cream at all times (label).

sources.name: DailyMed: SSD™ (1% Silver Sulfadiazine Cream) SSD AF™ (1% Silver Sulfadiazine Cream)
MedlinePlus: Silver Sulfadiazine
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-silver-sulfadiazine.note: Once or twice a day agrees (MedlinePlus); 12 h used as minimum interval.

med-chlorhexidine.dose_text: Rinse with 15 mL undiluted for 30 seconds twice daily, morning and evening after toothbrushing (label).

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Chlorhexidine Gluconate Mouth Rinse
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-chlorhexidine.note: Twice a day after brushing agrees (MedlinePlus). 15 mL is label-only (MedlinePlus gives no volume), so amount null. Skin-prep use not covered.

med-nystatin.dose_text: Label: 4-6 mL (400,000-600,000 units) four times daily, half in each side of mouth; hold in mouth before swallowing; continue 48 h after symptoms clear.

sources.name: DailyMed: Nystatin Oral Suspension USP [100,000 units per mL] I0868C0622 R06/22
sources.section: Dosage and Administration: Children and Adults

med-nystatin.note: MedlinePlus page section was incomplete in the fetched text, so no second-source confirmation; numeric fields null. Cream use not covered.

med-fluticasone-nasal.dose_text: Week 1: 2 sprays each nostril once daily; then 1-2 sprays each nostril once daily as needed (label).

sources.name: DailyMed: Perrigo Children’s 24-Hour Allergy Nasal Spray Drug Facts
MedlinePlus: Fluticasone Nasal Spray
sources.section: How should this medicine be used?

med-fluticasone-nasal.note: Once daily agrees (MedlinePlus, nonprescription). Spray count is label-only, so amount null.
